agree.reason: A judge reading this in ten minutes sees a clear request but trips over unfilled brackets for the clinic, the county, the matching funds and the reporting schedule, and never learns that one of the two current attorneys leaves in June, so the case for funding feels unfinished.

honest.reason: Most figures match the brief, but the '[80] additional tenants' estimate is not in the brief, and the claim that 60 days lets families move 'on their own terms rather than under the pressure of an immediate lockout' goes beyond the facts, since there is no figure for unrepresented tenants.

works_the_facts.reason: Working out the 14% representation rate and the $33,000 annual gap is useful, but the draft never sets the roughly 300 turned-away tenants against one attorney's capacity of about 80 cases, and never says what happens to capacity after June if nothing changes.

right_comparison.reason: The real alternative is a one-attorney clinic after June, with a five-month hiring lag, and the draft leaves that out; it also offers the 58% outcome rate with no comparison and doesn't admit that none exists.

qualification.reason: The October county renewal and the source of the matching funds are left as brackets instead of being stated as checkable conditions, and the draft drops the commitments to six-month reports and to requesting clerk outcome data in January.

objections.reason: A skeptical reviewer will ask whether the gap is really funded, whether the 58% means anything without a baseline, and whether the hire can be made in time; the $20,000 family-fund pledge and the departing attorney's training month answer the first and third questions, and neither appears in the draft.

fit.reason: It is under 300 words with clear section headings, but the many unfilled placeholders mean it can't be submitted as written.
